NOTE: The tumor has an unusual biphasic morphology composed of clusters of 
epithelial cells distributed evenly throughout a background of spindle cells. 
The epithelial cells form tubular glands and nests which are PR positive and 
keratin positive ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID / REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID , Pan-K, Cam REMOVED_DATE and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID /6). The spindle cells range 
from rounded to a more spindled appearance, have high grade nuclei, and these 
cells stain with keratin (Pan-K &  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID /6) as well as the myoepithelial markers 
p63 and calponin consistent with myoepithelial differentiation. The tumor has a 
lobulated border which is irregular and infiltrative. 
The staining pattern excludes an unusual phyllodes tumor. A malignant 
adenomyoepithelioma is favored given the distinctive morphological appearance 
and supporting immunostains. Although criteria which predict local recurrence 
and the development of distant metastases are not definitively established, 
available reports in the literature suggest that the presence of myoepithelial 
and epithelial nuclear pleomorphism and atypia, along with mitoses > REMOVED_DATE HPF, 
necrosis, and a lobulated or infiltrative border favors a diagnosis of 
"malignant adenomyoepithelioma". The two largest series have been published by 
Drs. Tavassoli and Page (see references below). Dr. S. Lester, & Dr. A. 
Richardson have also reviewed this case and agree with the diagnosis.

PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS: 
A. LEFT BREAST, PARTIAL MASTECTOMY ( REMOVED_CASE_ID g): 
Neutrophilic dermatitis with pan-dermal and subcutaneous involvement 
(see note) 
Fibroadipose tissue with acute inflammation and necrosis. 
Prior biopsy site. 
Breast parenchyma without specific primary pathological changes. 
A gram stain is negative for organisms; culture correlation 
is needed. 
B. LEFT BREAST, TISSUE, EXCISION: 
Neutrophilic dermatitis with pan-dermal and subcutaneous involvement 
(see note) 
COMMENT: 
Although it is difficult to exclude necrotizing fasciitis with certainty, the 
substantial pan-dermal infiltrate by neutrophils with associated superficial 
ulceration in the absence of primary endothelial occlusive alterations and 
zonal necrosis would favor pyoderma gangrenosum. The extent of subcutaneous 
involvement is, however, somewhat unusual for this entity, although secondary 
involvement from the overlying dermis and nature of sampling [debridement of 
more advanced regions] may in part account for this finding). It is 
recommended that the final diagnostic assessment also include consideration of 
correlative clinical parameters, notably exclusion of an infectious cause. In 
addition, if at anytime the clinical parameters continue to raise the 
possibility of necrotizing fasciitis (as opposed to an atypically deep/advanced 
manifestation of pyoderma gangrenosum), sampling of an early evolving lesion or 
lesion edge (as opposed to a debridement sampling) is suggested. 
Case referred by Surgical Pathology to Dermatopathology on REMOVED_DATE  and this 
diagnosis reflects this consultative review. 
CLINICAL DATA: 
History: None given. 
Operation: Left partial mastectomy (page 1) and debridement L breast and vac 
placement (page 2). 
Operative Findings: Not provided. 
Clinical Diagnosis: Necrotizing left breast infection (page 1) and necrotizing 
soft tissue infection L breast and chest wall (page 2). 
TISSUE SUBMITTED: 
A/1) left breast - long stitch/medial, short stitch/inferior periareolar. 
B/2) left breast tissue.

Part A, labeled "#1. Left breast", consists of a left partial mastectomy

(superficial to deep)cm ) with two orienting sutures ("long stitch medial; 
short stitch inferior periareolar"). The specimen is surfaced by a large, 
variegated brown, red, necrotic skin lesion which extends to multiple radial 
margins, with only a thin rim of tan, focally hyperemic epidermis (1.0cm in 
maximum thickness) predominantly at the superior aspect. At the upper inner 
quadrant, opening to the deep margin, is a necrotic cavity (7.5 x REMOVED_DATE x REMOVED_DATE 
cm). Approximately 6.5cm superior and lateral to the inferior suture (upper 
outer quadrant) is an ulcerating cavity (2.5 x REMOVED_DATE x 1.5cm ) which communicates 
with the skin, and is associated with a hemorrhagic biopsy site (0.9 x REMOVED_DATE x 
0.5cm ). The biopsy site comes to within 1.0cm of the deep margin and 
exhibits white synthetic material consistent with Gelfoam. A clip is not 
identified. The fibrous stroma adjacent to the biopsy site (approximately REMOVED_DATE 
x REMOVED_DATE x 2.7cm ) is diffusely granular/dense and extends to the deep margin 
(inked black). The remaining breast tissue exhibits necrosis adjacent to the 
skin extending approximately 1.5cm into the breast and soft tissue. The 
breast tissue is composed of approximately 85% yellow lobulated adipose tissue 
and 15% fibrous stroma. Axillary tissue is not present. No lymph nodes are 
identified.

Although it is difficult to exclude necrotizing fasciitis with certainty, the 
substantial pan-dermal infiltrate by neutrophils with associated superficial 
ulceration in the absence of primary endothelial occlusive alterations and 
zonal necrosis would favor pyoderma gangrenosum. The extent of subcutaneous 
involvement is, however, somewhat unusual for this entity, although secondary 
involvement from the overlying dermis and nature of sampling [debridement of 
more advanced regions] may in part account for this finding). It is 
recommended that the final diagnostic assessment also include consideration of 
correlative clinical parameters, notably exclusion of an infectious cause. In 
addition, if at anytime the clinical parameters continue to raise the 
possibility of necrotizing fasciitis (as opposed to an atypically deep/advanced 
manifestation of pyoderma gangrenosum), sampling of an early evolving lesion or 
lesion edge (as opposed to a debridement sampling) is suggested.

PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS: 
RIGHT BREAST SIMPLE MASTECTOMY: 
SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA OF LACTIFEROUS DUCTS with associated subareolar chronic 
granulomatous inflammation, see NOTE 
Uninvolved breast parenchyma with apocrine cysts. 
Skin with scar and prior procedure site changes. 
NOTE: Squamous metaplasia of lactiferous ducts (SMOLD) is also known as 
recurrent subareolar abscess and periductal mastitis. This unusual disease is 
mostly seen in smokers where it presents as a painful erythematous subareolar 
mass which fails to heal following incision and drainage of the "abscess". The 
pathology is keratinizing squamous metaplasia deep in the nipple ducts which 
causes them to dilate and then rupture producing a non-infectious chronic 
granulomatous inflammatory response (the "abscess") which often drains to the 
overlying skin as a purulent exudate via the offending nipple duct or a sinus 
tract. 
CLINICAL DATA: 
History: Chronic right breast infections 
Operation: RT simple mastectomy 
Operative Findings: Not provided 
Clinical Diagnosis: Not provided

measuring 23.0cm lateral to medial, 13.5cm superior to inferior, 5.0cm 
anterior to posterior. The specimen is covered by a skin ellipse, measuring 
13.5cm x 7.0cm with 3.0cm areola, centered by a 1.4cm everted nipple (0.7 
cm anterior to posterior). There is a 2.5cm well-healed scar in the lateral 
side of the areola. The nipple orifice oozes white thick purulent material. No 
additional fistula tracts are seen either on the areolar or on adjacent skin. 
The deep margin is an intact fascia and is inked black. Sectioning reveals a

nipple and 2.5cm from the deep margin. The entire nipple/areolar area to
